peptide.name: Mazdutide
peptide.summary: Mazdutide is a long-acting synthetic oxyntomodulin analog and dual agonist of the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, co-developed by Innovent Biologics and Eli Lilly. It is approved as a prescription drug in China for weight management but remains investigational in the United States, with no FDA approval as of this review.
peptide.description: Mazdutide (IBI362 / LY3305677) is a synthetic peptide analog of oxyntomodulin, a naturally occurring gut hormone with dual activity at the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and glucagon receptor (GCGR). Its peptide backbone incorporates a fatty-acyl modification that extends its in vivo half-life for once-weekly dosing. In published phase 3 Chinese trials, GLORY-1 (NEJM 2025) reported -12.55% body weight at 32 weeks with the 6 mg dose, and GLORY-2 (JAMA 2026) evaluated a 9 mg dose. A head-to-head phase 3 trial versus semaglutide 1 mg in early type 2 diabetes with obesity has also been conducted. Mazdutide has legal prescription status in China for weight management, making it one of the first drugs of its dual GLP-1/glucagon class to reach a regulatory market, but it remains investigational for the US market with no FDA approval. It is a distinct molecular entity from retatrutide (also Lilly-connected) and the two are not interchangeable; no head-to-head trial between them exists.
peptide.mechanism_of_action: Dual agonist at the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and glucagon receptor (GCGR), mimicking the natural gut hormone oxyntomodulin. GLP-1R activity enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, slows gastric emptying, and suppresses appetite; GCGR activity adds an energy-expenditure/thermogenic component not present in single GLP-1 agonists. Reported binding affinities: GCGR Ki of 17.7 nM (human) / 15.9 nM (mouse); GLP-1R Ki of 28.6 nM (human) / 25.1 nM (mouse); stimulates insulin secretion in mouse islets with an EC50 of 5.2 nM.
peptide.sequence: oxyntomodulin-analog backbone with fatty-diacid/PEG-linker modification (proprietary sequence)

half_life.note: Extended half-life consistent with once-weekly subcutaneous dosing used in trials, achieved via a fatty-acyl albumin-binding modification. Precise published half-life values were not confirmed in available sourcing.

peptide.evidence_note: Completed phase 3 trials primarily in Chinese populations (GLORY-1, published NEJM 2025; GLORY-2, JAMA 2026) demonstrated significant weight loss and support the China prescription approval. US-relevant, FDA-standard trial data are more limited; the drug remains investigational for the US market.
peptide.fda_status_note: NOT FDA-approved in the United States; investigational for the US market. Approved as a prescription drug (Rx) in China for weight management, based on completed phase 3 Chinese trials. Regulatory status differs meaningfully by jurisdiction -- do not assume US availability or approval based on the China approval.
peptide.compounding_note: Not FDA-approved in the US; not on the 503A bulks list; not eligible for legal US pharmacy compounding.

benefits.label: Significant weight loss (phase 3, China)
benefits.detail: GLORY-1 phase 3 trial reported -12.55% body weight at 32 weeks with the 6 mg dose; GLORY-2 evaluated a 9 mg dose with further reported benefit.

benefits.label: Glycemic improvement (phase 1b)
benefits.detail: Demonstrated safety and efficacy signals in Chinese adults with overweight/obesity and early type 2 diabetes in ascending-dose trials.

benefits.label: Dual mechanism energy-expenditure component (mechanistic)
benefits.detail: Combined GLP-1/glucagon agonism is proposed to add an energy-expenditure effect beyond single GLP-1 agonists.

risks.label: Limited US-population and long-term safety data
risks.detail: Most published trial data are from Chinese populations; long-term post-marketing safety data outside China are limited.

risks.label: GI tolerability
risks.detail: GI side effects common to incretin/glucagon-class drugs (nausea, diarrhea) reported in trials.

risks.label: Unregulated sourcing outside approved markets
risks.detail: Outside China's approved prescription channel, mazdutide obtained elsewhere is unregulated research-grade material.

contraindications.label: Personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2
contraindications.detail: Class-wide theoretical concern shared with other incretin-mimetic drugs pending mazdutide-specific labeling in each jurisdiction.

interactions.effect: Class-wide concern for increased hypoglycemia risk when combined with other glucose-lowering agents.

reconstitution.note: In approved/trial settings, supplied as a ready-to-use solution for subcutaneous injection. Research-grade lyophilized powder would be reconstituted with bacteriostatic water; concentration depends on diluent volume. Manufacturer guidance recommends freezer storage (-20C or below) for lyophilized material.

lyophilized.stability: Stable when kept frozen and dry (research-grade material).

reconstituted.stability: Refrigerate; use within a limited window.

peptide.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. Mazdutide is approved as a prescription drug in China but is NOT FDA-approved in the United States. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

dose_ranges.context: Phase 3 China trials (GLORY-1/GLORY-2) — reflects approved-jurisdiction trial dosing, not a US recommendation
dose_ranges.note: GLORY-1 evaluated 6 mg (-12.55% body weight at 32 weeks); GLORY-2 evaluated 9 mg. Reflects the dosing basis for China's prescription approval, not an FDA-approved or globally standardized dose.

protocols.name: Dose-escalation schedule (phase 3 China trial pattern)
protocols.description: Published trials titrate mazdutide upward over several weeks to the target weekly dose to manage GI tolerability, consistent with other incretin-class drugs. Summarized from trial design and the basis for China's approval; not an FDA-approved regimen.
protocols.cycling_notes: Chronic therapy pattern in trials, not cycled.
protocols.disclaimer: Summary of clinical trial design for educational reference. Not medical advice; not an FDA-approved dosing regimen.

related.note: Both are Lilly-connected multi-receptor metabolic agonists in active development; mazdutide is a dual GLP-1/glucagon agonist while retatrutide adds GIP receptor agonism as a triple agonist. No head-to-head trial exists between them.
Both are incretin-based metabolic therapies; mazdutide's phase 3 program included a head-to-head comparison against semaglutide in Chinese adults with early type 2 diabetes and obesity.
